facts.text: Princeton was named after its UK namesake and became the site of Princeton University, founded as the College of New Jersey in 1746.
Princeton’s recorded history begins in the late 17th century, when Lenni Lenape trails crossed the narrow 'waist' of New Jersey between the Delaware and Raritan rivers.
In 1756 the College of New Jersey moved from Newark, built Nassau Hall, and the village gained prominence and a strong Presbyterian influence.
Morven, once a private estate, now serves as a museum and garden operated by the New Jersey Historical Society.
On January 10, 1938, Henry Ewing Hale urged citizens to form the Historical Society of Princeton, preserving the town’s heritage.
The 1944 biographical film 'Wilson' about Woodrow Wilson used Princeton as a setting, though it was not filmed there.
